args.body:
Hi Dora! I just had a look at your personal website at www.dora-website.com. It's a nice, clean introduction, but right now it's really just a single line of text, so there's not much for a visitor to get a sense of who you are or what you do.

A few thoughts on how you could make it stronger:
- Add a short intro about yourself — what you do, what you're passionate about, or what you're working on. Even 2-3 sentences would help people connect.
- Include some recent posts, projects, or work samples with brief descriptions and links.
- Add a way to get in touch (a contact form or your email is already there, but making it a clickable link would help).
- A few photos or a simple layout with sections (About / Work / Contact) would make it easier to scan.

Overall it's a solid starting point — it loads fast and is easy to read. It just needs a bit more content to really shine. Nice to meet you on Slack!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I had a look at your blog at www.eve-blog.com. I love the personal touch — mentioning that hiking is your favorite hobby gives readers an immediate sense of who you are, and it feels like a great topic to build a blog around.

Some ideas to take it further:
- Add a few actual blog posts so there's something new for visitors to read and come back for.
- Since hiking is your passion, you could write about local trails, gear reviews, trip reports, or photo essays from your hikes.
- Organize things with categories or tags, and add an "About Me" section with a bit more background.
- An archive or "latest posts" list would help people find older content easily.
- If you share photos, adding captions and alt text makes the site more accessible.

The tone is warm and approachable, which is a nice foundation for a blog. Keep it up — I'd love to read more about your hiking adventures!

Best,
Emma Johnson
